paper.title: A Unifying Theory of Thompson Sampling for Continuous Risk-Averse Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: rho-MAB with multinomial arms on a finite alphabet
unmapped: Objective is maximisation of a risk functional rho(nu_k) (continuous and dominant, e.g. CVaR, proportional hazard, mean-variance) instead of the mean; regret is the rho-risk regret sum_k E[T_k(n)] (rho(nu_1)-rho(nu_k))
Rewards are multinomial on a known finite support S = {s_0,...,s_M} subset [0,1]; the learner knows the support S and the risk functional rho
settings.definition_quote:
Given a risk functional $ho$ on a compact metric subspace $({\ccal C},d) \subset ({\ccal P},d)$ of probability measures and $K$ arms with probability measures ${(
u_k)}_{k \in [K]} \subset {\ccal C}$, the learner's objective is to choose the optimal arm $k^* := \argmax_{k \in [K]} ho(
u_k)$ as many times as possible. ... ${\ccal R}_
u^{ho}(\pi, n) = \sum_{k=1}^K \EE_
u[T_k(n)] \Delta_k^{ho}$

settings.name_in_paper: rho-MAB over a product class of bandit models Q (lower bound)
unmapped: Objective is maximisation of a general risk functional rho(nu_k); regret is the rho-risk regret
Bandit model class Q = Q_1 x ... x Q_K of arbitrary distribution classes

source.label: thm: rho_lower_bound
source.quote:
Let ${\ccal Q} = {\ccal Q}_1 	imes \dots 	imes {\ccal Q}_K$ be a set of bandit models ... Let $\pi$ be any consistent policy. Suppose without loss of generality that $1$ is the optimal arm ... For any $
u \in \ccal Q$ and suboptimal arm $k$, $$\liminf_{n 	o \infty}  rac{\EE_
u[T_k(n)]}{\log n} \geq  rac{1}{{\ccal K}_{\inf}^{{ho},{\ccal Q}_k} (
u_k,r_1^ho)}.$$

results.notes: Per-arm pull-count lower bound; implies rho-regret lower bound sum_k Delta_k^rho log n / Kinf. Proof adapts Baudry et al. (2021). Quantity 'other' because it bounds pull counts under a risk-functional objective.

bound.expression_latex: {\ccal R}_\nu^{\rho}(\rho\text{-MTS}, n) \leq \sum_{k : \Delta_k^{\rho} > 0} \frac{\Delta_k^{\rho} \log n}{{\ccal K}_{\inf}^{\rho}(\nu_k,r_1^{\rho})} + o(\log n)

symbols.Kinf_rho_i: K_inf^rho(nu_i, r_1^rho) = inf{KL(nu_i, eta): eta in P_S, rho(eta) >= r_1^rho}

conditions: arms are multinomial on a fixed finite alphabet S = {s_0,...,s_M} subset [0,1]
rho is continuous on (P, D_inf) and dominant with |I| = M
quantity is the rho-risk regret sum_k E[T_k(n)] Delta_k^rho

source.label: thm: rho_mts_upper_bound
source.quote:
Fix a finite alphabet $\ccal S = \{s_0,s_1,\dots,s_M\} \subset C \subseteq [0,1]$. Let $
u$ be a $K$-armed bandit model. Let $ho$ be a continuous and dominant risk functional on $(\ccal P,D_\infty)$ such that $|\ccal I| = M$. Then the regret of $ho$-MTS is given by ${\ccal R}_
u^{ho}(ho	ext{-MTS}, n) \leq \sum_{k : \Delta_k^{ho} > 0}  rac{\Delta_k^{ho} \log n}{{\ccal K}_{\inf}^{ho}(
u_k,r_1^{ho})} + o(\log n)

results.notes: Leading term plus o(log n) recorded as limsup R/log n <= sum Delta/Kinf. Applies to CVaR, proportional hazard, lookback, expectation (any M) and convex EDPMs such as mean-variance for Bernoulli (M=1) per Remark 3. Horizon n is listed as an algorithm input though the TS update does not appear to use it.
